title: How StockAlarm hit ~$5.5K MRR bootstrapped: programmatic SEO, social bots and tiered pricing
summary: Yahia Bakour, head of growth at StockAlarm (B2C stock alert SaaS), explains how a part-time, bootstrapped team reached about 600 paying users and $5.5K MRR in a year. He covers reusing product data for social automation, a page per ticker for SEO, milestone-based equity for growth, and the pricing tier mistake he'd fix first.

principles.text: Turn data your product already has into free social content with automated bots.
principles.quote: we can reuse like we built this infrastructure, it has all this data, we want to reuse it. So, we built stuff like an automated Twitter bot that tweets out, you know, earnings info that we already have

principles.text: Build a programmatic SEO page for every entity (each ticker) and link it back to the marketing site.
principles.quote: we have like 12, 13,000 supported tickers. So, each one of those became its own page with its own SEO also linking to our marketing site. So, it just started boosting everything up.

principles.text: Win head-term keywords first through keyword research and steady optimization, then build backlinks.
principles.quote: We did our research on those keywords, and then we just kept optimizing until we grew.

principles.text: Stack cheap early channels: paid niche Instagram promos, Quora answers, social automation, then organic compounding.
principles.quote: We also did paid promotions with Instagram accounts target our dem our specific demographic. Uh we really put some money into ads there, answered Quora questions, so stuff like that. And then just kind of grew organically.

principles.text: Tie a growth hire's equity to user milestones so the reward tracks the work they control.
principles.quote: since I'm head of growth, the work I put in since we're barely any people, is directly correlated to the amount of users I bring in. So, they base it off how much the company's worth is how much equity I unlock.

principles.text: Launch pricing tiers from day one; adding them roughly doubled MRR almost instantly.
principles.quote: I wish we'd implemented pricing tiers from the start. The second we implemented it, we doubled our uh, MRR almost instantly.
